subject: Recap & cost anchors from today's PilgrimPay discovery
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emily Saunders <emily.saunders@pilgrimpay.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@pilgrimpay.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & cost anchors from today's PilgrimPay discovery

Hi Emily / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a set of cost anchors so you can compare against your budget assumptions. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Call summary (what we heard)
- Primary use case: real-time transaction scoring + fraud-explainability prompts for the payments UX (lightweight LLM responses embedded in checkout flows).
- Volume profile: ~20M transactions/month with model calls on 15% of events (rule + ML fallback), spike windows up to ~2.5x during peak campaigns.
- Latency requirement: P95 < 250ms for the front-end call (hard SLO).
- Data constraints: sensitive payment metadata, must be isolated; pilot can run in Redwood Dedicated or Private.
- Budget constraint: procurement indicated a mid-six-figure annual budget for the initial production roll; pre-sales needs a pilot-phase unit economics figure to present.

Key pain points you reiterated
1) Cost unpredictability with current hosted models (token-level billing spikes).
2) Latency variability at peak (leading to checkout failures).
3) Need for clear levers to trade cost vs. quality for exec sign-off.

Suggested cost anchors & levers (ballpark numbers)
- Baseline small-model path (quantized 7B): $0.0006 per token equivalent in dedicated mode after batching optimizations.
- Medium quality path (13B, mixed-precision): $0.0012 per token equivalent.
- Expected effective tokens per call (median UX prompt + response): 150 tokens.
- Estimated $/call (baseline): 150 * $0.0006 = $0.09.
- With 15% of 20M monthly events -> 3,000,000 calls/month -> ~$270k/month baseline (note: dedicated reserved discounts, caching can reduce this).

Batching & caching impact (recommended pilot levers)
- Continuous batching for background reranks — expect 30–50% per-token savings for non-interactive batches.
- KV/prefix caching for repeat prompts (checkout messages) — conservative 10–25% token reduction in steady state.
- Route low-risk calls to quantized-medium models during peaks for predictable throughput.

Immediate next steps (what we agreed)
1) I’ll send a one-page pilot scope + cost snapshot for procurement (attached).
2) Internal: if PilgrimPay can share a 1-week event sample (anonymized), Aditya will run a quick token-distribution estimate and return a refined cost projection.
3) Schedule a short follow-up next Wed to review the revised numbers and a sampling plan.

Attachments: PilgrimPay_pilot_scope_v1.pdf (scope + milestone checklist), token-econ-snapshot.xlsx (rough calc).

Appreciate the candor on budgeting — we’ll aim to show a clear path to < $X per month for the MVP profile.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for this, clear and helpful. A couple quick clarifications:
- The 15% call rate is our current estimate; could be as low as 10% depending on rule improvements.
- Our procurement asked for a 6-month runway estimate for pilot-to-prod conversion.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you provide a conservative scenario (no caching + minimal batching) and an optimized scenario (caching + aggressive batching) with monthly totals?
2) What are the minimum committed resources (GPU hours / reserved capacity) needed to hit P95 < 250ms at 2.5x peak?

If you can get a short doc to procurement by Monday, that would be ideal — they want something to review before a July 22 internal exec meeting.

Best,

Jasmine / Lauren —

Thanks for the context. Quick technical estimates below; I kept the math simple so we can iterate before sending to procurement.

Assumptions I used
- Median tokens per call: 150 (confirmable with a 1-week sample).
- Monthly calls: baseline 3M (15% of 20M), low 2M (10%), peak-multiplier 2.5x during campaigns.
- Models: 7B quantized (Q4_8) and 13B FP16 mixed.

Conservative scenario (no caching, minimal batching)
- 7B path: $0.0009/token effective (includes lower utilization, no caching) -> $0.135/call -> 3M calls = $405k/month.
- 13B path: $0.0018/token -> $0.27/call -> 3M calls = $810k/month.

Optimized scenario (KV caching + continuous batching)
- Batching + scheduling: expect ~40% token-cost reduction for non-latency-critical flows.
- KV/prefix caching: assume 15% token drop on interactive calls after warm-up.
- Effective 7B cost: $0.00054/token -> $0.081/call -> 3M = $243k/month.

Dedicated capacity guidance to hit P95 < 250ms at 2.5x peak
- For the 7B quantized path: a pool of 4 x A100-class GPUs with continuous batching and autoscale buffer should cover 2.5x peak (with conservative concurrency).
- For 13B mixed: recommend 6 x A100-class GPUs to maintain the same SLO.
- If privacy constraints push to Private on-prem, factor in ~15–25% infra overhead for isolation and fewer multi-tenant efficiencies.

Suggested content to send procurement Monday
- Two-line summary table (conservative vs optimized) with monthly totals and the 6-month projection.
- Short tech appendix with the dedicated capacity recommendation and privacy impact note.

I can produce the table today if you want me to drop numbers into the attached spreadsheet.
